newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in commercial market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in commercial market.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.04 percent to close at 1.0611 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market on dollar outflows and arbitrage between spot and future forex markets, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $20 million deficit on Thursday.
The real also fell due to some banks buying dollars in the commercial market and selling May forex future contracts, dealers added.

The spot market is currently expecting a total decline of around 0.60 percent in the reais-dollar mini-band this month and May contracts had been showing a 0.75 percent depreciation of the real against the dollar.
"There's room for further decline," a dealer said referring to the May contract, which closed at 1065.400 points on Thursday.

Some dealers were expecting a new decline in the mini-band on Friday. The current mini-band was set on Tuesday at between 1.0600 and 1.0650 reais per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered by 0.28 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real rose 0.02 percent to end at 1.0657 per dollar. In the parallel market, the real closed unchanged at 1.135 per dollar.
